system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

# Structural sub-dossier — Steadfast Income REIT, Inc. (closing-era organizational structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY how the entity's
> asset base was structured and expanded at the closing era — what crossed the ownership
> boundary and what did not. It contains no post-transaction outcome information.

## The drawn filing, described truthfully
- The drawn accession (0001468010-14-000044, Form 8-K, filed 2014-08-06) is not a
  deal-terms document. It reports the results of the Company's August 5, 2014 annual
  meeting of stockholders — election of directors, ratification of the independent
  auditor, and stockholder approval of a Third Articles of Amendment and Restatement —
  and separately notes that the Company filed those Third Articles with the Maryland
  State Department of Assessments and Taxation on August 6, 2014. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000044, Form 8-K Items 5.03/5.07]
- No merger, acquisition, or disposition of a business is described in this filing; it
  is a governance/charter event. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000044, Form 8-K]

## Nature of the entity and how its asset base was actually assembled
- The registrant is a Maryland corporation formed May 4, 2009, electing REIT status,
  that used the proceeds of a public non-traded stock offering (terminated December 20,
  2013) to invest in a portfolio of real estate, primarily multifamily properties,
  located throughout the United States. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013) Item 1]
- The registrant's real estate portfolio was assembled asset-by-asset over several
  years rather than through a single discrete corporate transaction: it owned eight
  multifamily properties at December 31, 2011, thirty at December 31, 2012, and
  sixty-three (comprising 15,859 apartment homes and 30,125 square feet of commercial
  space) at December 31, 2013. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013) Item 2]
- This asset-by-asset acquisition pattern continued into the closing era: on June 3,
  2014, through a newly formed, indirect wholly owned subsidiary (SIR Oak Crossing,
  LLC), the Company acquired from an unaffiliated third-party seller a fee-simple
  interest in a 222-unit multifamily community in Fort Wayne, Indiana for $24,230,000,
  financed with remaining IPO proceeds plus a $15,762,000 loan from PNC Bank under a
  Fannie Mae structured ARM program. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000026, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- No transitional-services, shared-services, or operating agreement with the property
  seller is described in connection with this acquisition; the acquired property was
  placed directly into the Company's own, already-standing external-management
  structure rather than bridged by an interim arrangement with the seller. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000026, Form 8-K]

## External advisor / property-manager tier and controlling-principal fusion
- The Company is externally managed: Steadfast Income Advisor, LLC (the "advisor")
  supervises and manages the Company's day-to-day operations and selects its real
  property investments, subject to board oversight. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013) Item 1]
- On March 12, 2014, the Company entered Amendment No. 5 to the Amended and Restated
  Advisory Agreement among the Company, its operating partnership, and the advisor,
  renewing the advisory relationship's term for one additional year (May 4, 2014 to
  May 3, 2015) — the same external-advisor structure was renewed, not replaced, going
  into the drawn filing's period. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000016, Form 8-K Item 1.01]
- Acquired properties are operated by Steadfast Management Company, Inc. (the
  "property manager"), an affiliate of the Company's sponsor, under management
  agreements paying a percentage-of-revenue fee; a small number of properties were
  managed instead by an unaffiliated third-party manager. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013) Item 1 / Item 13]
- The Company's sponsor, Steadfast REIT Investments, LLC, purchased the Company's
  initial shares in 2009 and is majority owned and controlled indirectly by Rodney F.
  Emery, who is also the Company's chairman and chief executive officer — a documented
  fusion of the controlling sponsor principal with the officer tier of the managed
  entity. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013) Item 13]

## Structural summary (closing era only)
- At the closing era, the entity's customer-facing product (leased multifamily real
  estate) crossed into the entity's ownership one asset at a time, from unaffiliated
  third-party sellers, financed by a mix of equity offering proceeds and asset-level
  mortgage debt; the operational processes and personnel that run each acquired asset
  were supplied throughout by the entity's own standing, sponsor-affiliated external
  advisor and property manager rather than inherited from the seller or bridged by a
  transitional-services agreement; and the controlling intent behind the entity was
  vested in a single natural person who was simultaneously the sponsor's controlling
  owner and the entity's chairman/CEO. [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000019, Form 10-K (FY2013)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001468010-14-000026, Form 8-K]

[SLICE END]
